Honestly not for me. I know the game is old and won't compare to modern titles today but the port is so unbelievably bad, There's just too many bugs and for the storyline a lot of the missions are just very dry.

I went into this game with very high expectations because of how much people praised it. I constantly heard that it's the best GTA game thanks to its dark, gritty atmosphere and more mature story.

Unfortunately, my experience couldn't have been more different.

This is easily one of the most frustrating GTA games I've ever played. The controls are incredibly clunky and unresponsive. Yes, the physics are impressive, and the parkour mechanics are a nice idea, but none of that matters when simply controlling your character feels like a struggle.

The game also boasts a lot of enterable buildings, but most of them are completely empty, making the world feel less interactive than it first appears.

As for the missions, I kept playing because everyone said the story was worth it. Instead, I spent hours doing repetitive "go here, kill these people, mission complete" objectives. To make matters worse, the lack of mission checkpoints means that if you fail because of the game's awkward controls, you're forced to replay the entire mission from the beginning.

I gave the game 11 hours because I genuinely wanted to see what everyone was talking about. I kept waiting for it to get better, but eventually I ran out of patience. It became more exhausting than enjoyable, which was disappointing given all the praise and the high expectations I had going in.

And finally, I can't ignore the optimization. This is one of the worst-optimized games I've ever played.

Requires 3rd party non-steam workshop mod "FusionFix" otherwise game is very unstable. However its a very easy drag and drop mod install. Would also recommend turning off aim assist even with controller because the 1-shot headshot mechanic is very satisfying but the auto aim defaults to torso. 

Great game though once fixed. I watched both the брат movies in uni and it really feels like there was a big inspiration taken from those movies in a good way. Niko is probably the most righteous of all gta protags; just a loyal soldier who came to America to be closer to his brother whose been bragging about living the rich life in the states, just to find out his brother is broke and drowning in the criminal world and only when Niko tries to protect his family is he then entwined into the criminal world.

Here is the deal. This is a fantastic game and a terrible port that is fundamentally broken.
If you're fine with modding the game to fix most of the issues. This is absolutely worth it. 

However, since Rockstar/Take2 are selling it in a state this broken and besides shoving in their Rockstar Social Launcher/Account thingy and patches that broke some visual effects. I can't give it a thumbs up.

When it comes to the game itself. The story is imho the best in the series. The driving is the most satisfying. The gunplay and features are serviceable but nothing special. The atmosphere is superb. 
When using some of the biggest fixes, the graphics hold up fairly ok for what used to be a Xbox 360/PS3 game at one point.

Performance is very iffy without mods. On Linux it runs a bit better than on Windows, thanks to DXVK. DXVK however, can also be applied when playing it on Windows, albeit requiring a bit more tinkering.

At the time of writing this (July 2026), when using the mods "FusionFix", "VariousFixes", "Radio Restoration" and "Console Visuals" you could get a pretty decent experience, playing at a mostly stable 60fps without some of the nasty glitches and broken visuals while also restoring the intended atmosphere.

Conclusion: If you're ok with modding, get it on a sale and it'll probably be worth it. If you don't want to tinker at all, don't bother and maybe wait for a remaster, which could end up as broken as this, if not worse and they might possibly remove this version from the store.

citations.review_text:
I've been meaning to finish this for so long. I never did get all the way through back when it came out. I found it too serious, nothing like my favourite GTA VC. Running it on Linux has been perfect, the PC port is known for bad performance and I haven't seen any of that.

I just hate the Rockstar launcher system.

GTA4 is a weird game to quantify but despite it being arguably the best GTA game and the gold standard for open world games I don't love it.
More verbose and autistic individuals than me have made many (many) arguments to GTA4s greatness and I would agree with most points; GTA4 is incredibly ambitious, it improves upon most of the systems from the '3D' trilogy and has an insane attention to detail which mostly add to the experience.
I feel like my two takeaways from replaying this game is that fun has been somewhat sacrificed on the alter of realism and almost every character you interact with is a giant c#ck.
The story, and your protagonist are generally narratively strong although some of the 'crime doesn't pay' and 'bad people are victims of their history' moral grandstanding comes across as heavy-handed and repetitive especially after the *big story plot point* happens towards the end of the game.
Additionally, this version IMO requires a certain amount of modding to play smoothly on modern systems as rockstar/TakeTwo only really care about money.
Also, the rockstar launcher and the forcing of people to sign up to a third party account to play is anti-consumer and frankly cancerous capitalist sh#te.
In short, better than GTA5 not as good as San Andreas worth your time in general.
(Also also better than spending £90 on GTA6.)

Unfortunately I cannot recommend any games from Rockstar. When I had originally signed up for an account with Rockstar, I signed up with a Comcast email that I no longer have access to and that is no longer even active. This email was linked from my Rockstar account to my Steam account. As a result, I am no longer able to play any of Rockstar's games on Steam. When you start the game, you are required to sign in through Rockstar's launcher and you have to verify your account by them sending a code to your email. I no longer have access to that email, so I am not able to verify my account. 

THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO WORKAROUND FOR THIS

I have contacted Rockstar support multiple times to try and fix this, but they close out the support tickets saying that I am not providing enough information, or that I am not putting a ticket through the account that I no longer have access to. Rockstar does not care though, because they are such a huge company, they can afford to lose customers. I suppose they just want me to create a new Steam account and buy their games again, but I am not going to do that. I am very disappointed with Rockstar's customer service. I have bought all of their games MULTIPLE TIMES since the release of GTA III, and they cannot even help fix this small problem. All they have to do is let me link a new email to my Steam account, but they are not willing to do this.

Just be aware if you link your Rockstar account to your Steam account, you have to make sure you keep access to the email account that is linked, because otherwise you will not be able to play any of their games on Steam.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the story as dark, serious, and centered around Niko Bellic's revenge and immigrant background in Liberty City.

citations.review_text:
Everyone owns GTA V but I wanted to try and go back and play the previous entries in the series. My start? GTA IV. I think GTA IV is a good game, but I wouldn't necessarily call it great. The main drawback is that I don't think it's aged particularly well in the graphics and gameplay department, but I don't really think I can hold a 2008 game up to 2026 standards (obviously). I like Niko as a protagonist though and enjoyed going on his revenge quest. There is your quintessential cast of goofy GTA characters, but, to me, none stuck super well - except for Roman, of course. Solid game. 

"Niko, it's Roman. Let's go bowling"
7/10

The step up in realism is felt immediately. Liberty City and NY being 1:1 is hilarious. Each borough highlights this, and hosts their own set of colorful characters unique to the area. The only Russian clothing shop being in Hove (not Brighton) Beach hits the sardonic satire R* are specialist at. 

Narratively, its my favorite GTA story and character. While Vice City and San Andreas had obvious film influences, this was a story of revenge and immigrant identity bespoke to Liberty City.

Shame I had to use mods to get it up and running however a true gem and masterpiece in its own right.

[spoiler] and I will say...killing Darko and then taking the deal is exactly what real Niko would do. After traveling to Liberty City to avenge his comrades, no matter the condition Darko was found in, that had to be done. After his comments of emptiness and that car ride in silence made me think he was ready to move on with his new life. That ultimately yields a nightmare ending which I think fits right into this world. [/spoiler]

my favorite gta game, up there with san andreas. honestly both iv and sa are just as great in my opinion, for different reasons. but gta iv is my new favorite from the series.

iv in particular i think has the best story in the series (though not as iconic as sa's), and i don't think we will be getting a gta story this dark and in-depth again.

it's still pretty fun and wacky, it's not all dark, all the time. but there's a lot of emotion here, and a lot of moments that resonated with me. niko is my favorite gta character for sure, and i love his character depth.
Best GTA, not like GTA V with the clown story, GTA IV is more serious, for adults, not 12 year olds.

GTA IV isn't just my favorite Grand Theft Auto. It's my favorite Rockstar game ever made. 100/10 hands down!

People will always say GTA V is bigger, more polished, or more modern. That's fine. None of that makes it better.

GTA IV has something almost no other open-world game has: soul.

Liberty City feels cold, dirty, depressing, and believable. It isn't trying to be a playground where everything is a joke. It feels like a city full of broken people trying to survive.

Then there's Niko Bellic. In my opinion, he's Rockstar's greatest protagonist. He's not a stereotypical action hero or a wisecracking criminal. He's a war veteran carrying trauma that never leaves him. Throughout the game, you hear pieces of his past in conversations that are genuinely disturbing. He talks about the horrors he witnessed during the war and the things he was forced to become. Those moments completely change how you see him. You realize this isn't someone chasing the American Dream. It's someone trying to outrun memories that refuse to let him go.

Even the smallest details tell a story. The way Niko calmly reacts during violent moments, the way he handles a weapon, the way he carries himself... none of it feels exaggerated. It feels like someone who's done terrible things for far too long. Rockstar didn't need to explain everything. They trusted the player to notice.

And then there are the physics.

Almost 20 years later, GTA IV still has some of the most satisfying vehicle physics I've experienced. Cars have weight. They slide, roll, and react to the road in a way that still feels more believable than many modern open-world games. I've played games like Cyberpunk 2077, racing games, and countless other open-world titles, and I still find myself coming back to GTA IV because driving simply feels right.

The atmosphere is unmatched. The writing is mature. The soundtrack is incredible. The attention to detail is obsessive. Every corner of Liberty City feels handcrafted.

Rockstar shoul…

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that the game lacks meaningful ways to spend money earned during the later stages of the campaign.

citations.review_text:
Although I'm a big fan of the GTA series, until now I had only played the III-VC-SA trilogy, and after many years I finally decided to give GTA IV a chance. It has the familiar feeling of the older GTA games while improving many aspects, such as the combat system, the liveliness of the open world, the vehicle models, and more.
What impressed me the most is how successfully the game portrays the corruption and decay of Western/American society of that era (with the usual doses of satire and exaggeration the series is known for), where mafias, corruption, drugs, and authoritarian policing are everywhere. This is reflected perfectly through the foggy, gloomy environments and the many poorly built and ugly neighborhoods that show poverty and misery.
On the other hand, the world feels very realistic. It doesn't feel obvious that NPCs are just walking around following simple patterns like in the older games. They feel much more alive: they are busier during the morning, they exercise in parks, carry coffee, food, and umbrellas when it rains, and generally make the city feel alive.
And during those rare moments when the sun finally comes out, the whole city lights up and suddenly you get a feeling that everything is going to be alright... until the next slap of harsh reality hits you!
One big negative for me is that by the time you finish the story you have collected a lot of money, but there is almost nothing meaningful to spend it on besides clothes, weapons, and hospital bills every time you die, which are surprisingly expensive (another realistic, although very annoying, touch).

The atmosphere of this game is the only thing that carries it nowadays. I understand that this was the first game in the HD universe of GTA and Rockstar was traying new things out. The game was probably pretty revolutionary at the time of the release and im sure that many of you have played it back then (like myself), but it simply isnt good enough to play right now.

1. This point is the most crucial one - the game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring. Every single mission is the same, I started going insane while playing through main story line. -Drive all the way across the map in a vechicle that seems to weigh like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tank, watch a cutscene, and? - oh wow, an ambush! What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ surprise! I definetly havent seem the same plot 30 times already! -Now go kill everybody and drive some guy home. Thats the essence of the game for you, nothing ever changes.

2. Alredy touched on this point above but anyways. -The driving is horrendous. It feels like you are driving a dumbell on an ice rink. The only viable vechicles are supercars but most of the times you will be forced to drive some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ SUV that accelerates like a turtle and cant turn properly.

3. There is absolutley no incentive to earn money. What are you gonna do with hundreds of thousands of dollars? -buy a hotdog and some shoes?! You cant buy cars, you cant buy property, you cant gamble, so whats even the point? They could so many ways to spend money but they didnt.

4. Guns feels like cheap airsoft replicas. The euphoria ragdolls are quite fun but the guns themselves are rather dull. After you get an AK there is no point in using any other weapons. There is also no customisation whatsoever, and im not even talking about some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ skins, although they could add some camos that would break the immersion, but what the definetly couldve added are attachments. Like silencers, scopes, extended mags, underbarrel grenade launchers, etc.

5. There are no cloud saves. I played through half of the game on my steamde…

This game is not only the weakest of all the GTA titles to date, it's also one of the most mid games I've suffered through to date.  One of the highest flaws of this game is the glitches, there's 3 times I've encountered game breaking bugs that I had to find work arounds to get past.  The last game breaking bug was on the final mission that's a marathon of a quest (and if you mess up at any point, you have to restart the whole thing) which caused me to lose any care in completing the game.

The next massive critique I have is that towards the end where you're swimming in money, you have nothing to spend it on.  There's no properties, there's no cars, there's nothing.  The final massive critique is the constant interruptions from the npcs demanding you hang out with them, or they get mad at you.  Especially towards the end when you're just trying to complete a game you're already burnt out on and you hear "NIIIIKOOOOO, MY COUSIN!!!! LETS GO TO THE STRIP CLUB!"

The storyline is mid at best.  Without spoilers, it's a snowball of a story focused on revenge that just keeps rolling and getting bigger.  The vast majority of characters are either forgettable or obnoxious with only a few that stand out as being okay.  The "better" missions in the game feel repetitive, and the "bad" missions are noticeable with vehicles, npcs that cannot be killed until you've followed them for x amount of time.  It's a massive step down from San Andreas and it's no wonder that GTA V hit as hard as it did after this lemon of a game.

I genuinely cannot fathom how people enjoy this game, let alone give it a positive rating.

Greatest GTA of all time. The story is so good that it doesnt need a garage for your cars, gambling, or gun customization. Its just too damn good. We will NEVER have another GTA like this ever again. All the creators of this arent at rockstar anymore. Also, its so not PC. This game is something very special made during a time when men could say, do, and be how they wanted to be.

Thats GTA IV

Aside from all the bugs i've encountered, and crashes, finishing the main story, this game truly lives up even after 18 years. don't really like that if we fail the mission we have to replay it again from the beginning.
an important bug that caused me problems, is in the last mission, where niko has to climb the helicopter by tapping rappidly space bar.  problem is you have to get your game locked to 30 fps, because of outdated updates and game engine not registering the action.

In my opinion, the best GTA of the series, but this port isn't great. I recommend you either mod this version to fix some of its issues, or simply play it on the Xbox 360 or PS3 (I recommend the 360 for it preforms far better as far as I remember).

The dark and serious story is great, and the physics are so much fun. The car physics are hard to get used to at first, but at least for me, clicked later and felt great. 

The no autosaving during missions are a real pain to deal with in the older GTAs. I've had it where I'll start a mission, almost fully complete it, but die in the most stupidest way, and then be sent to a hospital and have to drive all the way back to the mission location and start it from the beginning. It sometimes lets you retry the mission from your phone, but weirdly only sometimes appeared for me.

This game is about £5 on sale. even if your not planning on playing the story, the game itself is generally so much fun, and so unique for a GTA, or even any game in general to be honest. 

The music is iconic, and the City is even more iconic. 

Rockstar, PLEASE add the Euphoria physics into GTA VI? please.

I've spent much time just living in Liberty City, and not doing any story. I very much recommend this game. In my opinion, it's the best Grand Theft Auto to date.

cohorts.summary: Long-term players point out ongoing launcher sign-in hurdles, poor port optimization requiring community mods, and a final mission sequence that demands manual framerate limits due to a lack of checkpoints.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the PC port suffers from poor optimization, bugs, and performance issues, and recommend installing community mods like FusionFix to ensure a stable experience.

citations.review_text: For the best playing experience, be sure to install FusionFix. This rids the game of the common bugs Rockstar never cared to fix themselves, as well as including a few improvements.
One of the best gta games. Bad pc port though..

Quite possibly the best GTA ever made. The Euphoria physics make this game really fun to play or just mess around in. Niko Bellic is honestly the best protagonist, with a really tragic backstory. The writing is mostly serious, but it can get funny sometimes. Really memorable.
The DLCs are amazing as well. Luis comes very close to Niko as my favorite protagonist, and playing as Johnny is very bittersweet, knowing what happens to him in 5.

The game and it's PC port are pretty outdated though, so sadly you need to mod it, but it's very easy. Just get FusionFix, and if you want slightly more HD textures you can do that as well.

"Where's luxury condo, where's sports car? Where's Barbara with big titties and Stephanie who sucks like a vacuum?" - Niko

please mod the game if you buy it. on keyboard and mouse the base game if you have loads of FPS then your aim will jitter you need to mod it to get the best experience as the port of the game wasn't very good at all
Peak game, runs bad without mods but with mods it is 100/10.

After almost 20 years of modding community work, this game can finally show itself in the best light where it's worthy of recommendation to any PC gamer. The FusionFix takes care of everything Rockstar's mediocre port didn't, and there are even mods to restore the music Rockstar deleted.

With all of this in mind, this is the definitive edition of the game that's the closest to the vanilla vision of the developers. I completed the game multiple times over the last 15 years, and the last time with all the fixes was the most enjoyable. It's a shame it took this long to get to enjoy this game in its full glory.

Hell, it even runs better on Linux than on Windows thanks to Proton and DXVK.

I mostly play this game for LCPDFR and I've been playing that mod for just over 7 years now, however I have played about half of the story and so far the vanilla game is absolutely amazing, it's geniunely the best Grand Theft Auto game I've ever played, for those who think GTA 5 is the best, they need to sit down and play this game whether it's on the Xbox 360/PS3 or the PC Version.

however there are a list of issues I have with the game despite being the best in the series:

1. Bugs; however most of the game breaking bugs are fixed, there's still some bugs that you can find within the game
2. Poor Optimisation; geniunely the worst optimisation in any Rockstar Game I've ever seen
3. Updates/Bug Patches don't do ♥♥♥♥; none of the updates do anything at all these days, one update was so infamous because it broke ♥♥♥♥.
4. Rockstar ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up the modding community; with the update that merges both IV and EFLC into one package, most if not all mods don't work on the latest patch, only thing you can mod in is custom vehicles, peds, weapons, etc however the infamous taxi bug still exists in the latest from what I remember (fact check me on that)
5. No Multiplayer/Online; this is self explanatory, like seriously Rockstar, why the ♥♥♥♥ is there no Multiplayer? due to this we have to rely on downgrading the game to 1.0.8.0 if you don't plan on playing LCPDFR Multiplayer, or you could use Grand Theft Auto Connected.
6. Some Achievements are unobtainable unless you downgrade; for those achievement hunters out there who wants to 100% GTA IV, well I'm sorry you're ♥♥♥♥ outta luck, due to the fact that you can't access the Police Computer without connecting to the GFWL Servers, you cannot obtain all achievements, I accidentally obtained these achievements when CE decided to load my 100% save I use on 1.0.7.0 for LCPDFR so I can have access to all islands

citations.review_text: If you registered with rockstar 18 years ago when this game came out on an email you dont have access to anymore, you are 100% screwed. you will never be able to play this game again as of rockstar's addition of the launcher to this title. I would like my game back please.

This is a gem. A crude history with good characters. Another redemption game made by rockstar, but at the end any decision you make you will feel like you didn't made the right choice. 

You can skip the motorcycle DLC, the main character is a ******ker , really. I feel so bad for his interaction in GTA V, but i guess he reaped what he sow. 
Ballad of Gay Tony, it's funny, that's all.

Bad side:
* Rockstar Launcher
* Bad port to pc
* Rockstar banning mods 
* Rockstar

GTA 4 is a prime example on what all Rockstar Games should be. The dark atmosphere to the game gives it a nice and unique touch. I loved playing through all of the different campaigns as Niko, Johnny and Luis. Their stories were quite enamouring and lacked any of that woke pandering ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that no one wanted. Rockstar didn't even hold back on any of the small details present in this game. Especially when the radio glitches whenever you get a phone call. That was very nostalgic.

I got to admit, GTA 4 was definitely living ahead of its time and it was totally worth it on replaying the entire game. It was quite refreshing to play this game during a time where 90% of game companies have now gone to ♥♥♥♥. This game will forever hold a special place in my heart, even if you need the Rockstar Social Club to run it.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the final mission features a quick-time sequence that fails if the CPU is not artificially limited, requiring players to restart from the beginning due to a lack of checkpoints.

citations.review_text:
Flaws aside, game is relatively playable until the very end, which is almost unbeatable. In the final mission, there is a quick time sequence which requires you to limit CPU, otherwise the engine freaks out and you inevitably fail and have to restart from scratch, since checkpoints somehow aren't a thing in this game. If you manage to get past that part, you have to deal with the unintuitive helicopter controls that require two hands to pilot it (the vehicle physics in this game are notoriously sluggish and difficult to control) and a third hand in order to simultaneously fire the attached miniguns, which is required. 

Good luck not crashing into the river.
Really good story, Excellent gunplay, Excellent driving. overall an 9/10 (some of the missions at the end were so hard they had me tweaking so one point off)
